headline: Google and Constellation Energy announced nuclear power deals totalling 3,590 megawatts, but only 890 megawatts of that is new capacity.
score_reason: Pool score 6 lowered by 1: the deal is from 6 Oct 2026 and was carried on 7 Oct; today's article adds analysis, not a new event.
importance_line: It matters first to electricity users on the PJM grid, where the grid's independent market monitor says data-centre demand is the main reason capacity fell 6,831 megawatts short of its reliability target in the 2028-2029 auction, then to regulators who must approve each upgrade, and to Google and Constellation, but the price and other commercial terms are private and the added power arrives only between 2028 and 2032.
source: Global Data Center Hub, citing Constellation Energy and Google
summary: Global Data Center Hub, an industry newsletter, reports, citing announcements by Constellation Energy and Google on 6 Oct 2026, that a 20-year contract backs 890 megawatts of added output from upgrading 11 existing reactors in Illinois, Pennsylvania and New Jersey to raise their licensed output, with Constellation saying it will invest more than $4.3 billion, while a separate 15-year contract keeps 2,700 megawatts of existing supply running on PJM, the largest US power grid. Added since our 7 Oct edition, which carried the deal, the newsletter's analysis stresses that only about a quarter of the 3,590-megawatt total is new power, that each upgrade still needs approval from the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission, and that the first upgrade is expected by 2028 and all 890 megawatts before the end of 2032.
notes: Repeat of a story carried on 7 Oct 2026; expect the 14-day duplicate check to hold it back. Google's claim of no cost to other ratepayers is a company claim and is not in the summary.
